ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Belinda is building squares with matches, adding small squares to those already built according to the figure. How many matches does she have to add to the 30th square to build the 31st?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows square patterns built with matches; the one labeled 1 is a 1×1 small square; the one labeled 2 is a 2×2 small square grid composed of shared edges; the one labeled 3 is a 3×3 small square grid composed of shared edges. Therefore the nth figure can be regarded as an n×n small square grid. Reasoning: In an n×n grid, in the horizontal direction there are n+1 rows, each row has n matches, for a total of n(n+1) matches; in the vertical direction there are also n+1 columns, each column has n matches, for a total of n(n+1) matches. So the total number of matches is 2n(n+1). The number of matches that needs to be added to change from the 30th figure to the 31st figure is 2·31·32 - 2·30·31 = 1984 - 1860 = 124.

Then the number added to go from the 30th to the 31st figure is total(31) - total(30) = 2·31·32 - 2·30·31 = 124.
